title: Proper coincidence of compact-support and ordinary cohomology
statement:
In the notation of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], if $Y$ is
proper then the
compact-support direct image and the ordinary direct image agree,

$$
Ra_{Y!}\cong Ra_{Y*},
$$

so that $H_c^i(Y,K)\cong H^i(Y,K)$ for every $K$.

proof.text: Use the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. In particular $Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. Since $Y$ is proper over $k$, $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $c_0=(\operatorname{id}_Y,a_Y)$ is a compactification by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $j=\operatorname{id}_Y$, every object $V\to Y$ factors through $j$, so the presheaf defining $j_!M$ in [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is exactly $M$, on sections, restriction maps and morphisms; it is already a sheaf. Hence $j_!$ is naturally the identity, including on complexes. The formula of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] therefore gives $Ra_{Y!,n}^{c_0}\cong Ra_{Y*,n}$ for every $n\geq1$. Bounded constructible finite-coefficient objects have etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] identifies the compactification-independent functor with this value on its required domain; its identity and cocycle clauses make this identification natural and independent of a common refinement.

source.place: first paragraph, through the finite-level identification and compactification independence

proof.text: For integral coefficients choose $c_0$ at every level in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$. The two towers defining $Ra_{Y!}K$ there and $Ra_{Y*}K$ in [def-weil-derived-direct-image] have the same terms $\operatorname{Res}_n Ra_{Y*,n}K_n$. Their transition maps also agree: [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] specifies the compact-support coefficient comparison as $j_!\operatorname{Res}=\operatorname{Res}j_!$ followed by the ordinary derived-direct-image coefficient comparison. For $j=\operatorname{id}_Y$ the first map is the identity on every section, so both transitions are the same reduction map $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}K_n$ followed by the same ordinary coefficient comparison. Thus the tower identifications commute with every transition, and taking the derived limit of this identical diagram yields $Ra_{Y!}K\cong Ra_{Y*}K$, naturally in $K$.

source.place: first paragraph, passage from all finite coefficient levels to the integral functor

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] use the rationalized category of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Apply localization to the integral isomorphism and its inverse: on a morphism $u\otimes a$ its naturality equation is the integral naturality equation for $u$ multiplied by $a\in E$. The two composites remain identities, giving $Ra_{Y!}\cong Ra_{Y*}$ over $E$. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, use [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: on an object $(E,K_E)$ take the isomorphism over $E$, and on a morphism represented over a common extension $L$ use its naturality equation over $L$. The finite-level comparisons above are identities after choosing $c_0$, so extension of coefficients sends each comparison to the comparison for the extended coefficients. Consequently these equations agree after every further extension and define a natural isomorphism in the common-stage category. This treats all four coefficient rings in the statement's notation.

source.place: first paragraph, the functor identification for rational and algebraically closed coefficients

proof.text: For each coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], apply $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ to the isomorphism $Ra_{Y!}K\cong Ra_{Y*}K$ and its inverse. Their composites remain identities. The displayed definitions give $\RGammac(Y,K)\cong\RGamma(Y,K)$. Applying the degree-$i$ cohomology functor to these two inverse maps again gives inverse maps, hence $H_c^i(Y,K)\cong H^i(Y,K)$ for every integer $i$. For a Weil complex the same assertion applies to its underlying complex, as stipulated in that definition.

source.place: first paragraph, from applying Fib_s to the final cohomology conclusion

blueprint_update.statement:
In the notation of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], if $Y$ is
proper then the
compact-support direct image and the ordinary direct image agree,

$$
Ra_{Y!}\cong Ra_{Y*},
$$

so that $H_c^i(Y,K)\cong H^i(Y,K)$ for every $K$.

proof.text:
If $Y$ is proper, the identity is a compactification of the structure
morphism $a_Y$, namely
$Y\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}Y\xrightarrow{a_Y}\Spec k$
with $a_Y$ proper, so at every finite coefficient level
$Ra_{Y!,n}=Ra_{Y*,n}$ by
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and the comparison maps of
that definition are identities for the identity refinement; hence the
compactification-independent functor $Ra_{Y!}$ is naturally
identified with the ordinary derived direct image $Ra_{Y*}$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Applying the equivalence
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] to both sides gives
$\RGammac(Y,K)\cong\RGamma(Y,K)$, hence
$H_c^i(Y,K)\cong H^i(Y,K)$ for every $K$, by the definitions of the
ordinary and compactly supported cohomology groups in
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].
